input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The OR composition checks for retry_all when deciding whether to flatten an existing retry_any.
- failure path: with `(A & B) | C`, the retry_all on the left is spliced into the retry_any as if it were a plain list of predicates, so the combination behaves as `A | B | C`: a retry fires when only A holds although the author required A and B together; no error is raised and the extra retries are silent

Reviewer finding
- description: The async retry_any.__ror__ flattens when `other` is a retry_all, merging its sub-retries into an OR group. That changes the meaning of the expression.
- rationale: Trigger: `(retry_if_a & retry_if_b) | retry_if_c` in the asyncio module, where the left side is a retry_all. The left operand goes to retry_any.__ror__ with other=retry_all, so it returns retry_any(A, B, C). The intended result is any(all(A, B), C). A retry that should require both A and B now fires when only A holds, so retries happen when they should not. The sync retry.py version checks isinstance(other, retry_any) correctly, so the two modules diverge.
critique: The finding names the same faulty check: the OR composition flattens when the other operand is a retry_all instead of a retry_any. It also gives the same consequence, `(A & B) | C` behaving as `A | B | C`, so retries fire when only A holds. The mechanism and the failure path both match the label.
